:J U D G M E N T:

This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest for the damage caused to Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MK-6492 in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 16.12.2022.

2. The averments of the petition in brief is as follows:
On 16.12.2022 at about 11.30 a.m., petitioner was driving the Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MK-6492 slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic norms.

When he was proceeding near Pakashala Hotel, Kudur Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagara D i s t r i c t o n B a n g a l o r e - M a n g a l o r e N H - 7 5 r o a d , t h e c a r b e a r i n g Reg.No.KA-51-ML-0699 came in a reverse direction without any indication with high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's car.
Due to said impact, the front portion of the petitioner's car was completely damaged.
He was earning a sum of Rs.60,000/- from the said vehicle and due to damages caused to his vehicle, he has sustained loss of Rs.4,50,000/-.
The accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of Car Reg.No.KA-51-ML-0699 by its driver.
In this regard the case has been registered by the Kudur police against the driver of offending vehicle.
At the time of accident, the 1 st respondent is the insurer and the 2nd respondent is the R.C. Owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, both the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.
3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the 1st respondent/insurer appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
The 2nd respondent/R.C. owner appeared through his counsel and failed to file written statement.

4. The written statement averments of the 1st respondent are hereunder:
This respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-ML-0699.

Inter-alia contended that, the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy, valid and effective driving licence possessed by the driver of offending vehicle, valid permit and fitness certificate.
It is contended that, there is no compliance of 134(c) of M.V.Act and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further contended that, the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-ML-0699 was not possessed valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Hence, the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy by entrusting his vehicle to the said driver.

This respondent has denied the accident, involvement of the above said Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-ML-0699 in the accident, damages caused Rajesh Prabhu M vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12171043/
2 to the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MK-6492 in the accident, amount spent towards repair of said Car.

sentences.text: Inter-alia contended that, the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-ML-0699 was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of above offending Car.
The petitioner was driving his car without having DL, without taking any proper precautions and indication and suddenly came in a zig zag manner.
Hence, the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner alone.
With these contentions, 1st respondent prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following issues have been framed:
:ISSUES:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 16.12.2022, at about 11.30 a.m., while he was driving the Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MK-6492 on NH-75,
Bangalore-Mangalore road, near Hotel Pakashala, Kudur Hobli, Magadi Taluk,
Ramanagara, his car was severally damaged due to rash or negligent driving of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-ML-0699 by its driver as stated in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the reliefs sought for? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself examined as P.W.1 and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
Further, he examined one witness as P.W.2.
P.W.1 and P.W.2 were cross- examined from the side of respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 did not chosen to lead evidence.
7. Heard the arguments from both side.
Perused the records placed before the Tribunal.

The findings of this Tribunal to the above referred Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 :- In the Partly Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :- As per the final order, for the following:

:REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1 :- In order to prove his case, petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
In order to prove issue No.1, P.W.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6.
Accordingly, Ex.P.1 is the true copy of complaint.
Ex.P.2 is the true copy of FIR pertaining to Cr.No.544/2022.
Ex.P.3 is the true copy of spot mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is the true copy of M.V.A. report.
Ex.P.5 is the true copy of charge sheet.

Ex.P.6 is the notarized copy of R.C.

sentences.text: According to the petitioner, his Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MK-6492 was damaged in the road accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-Ml-0699.

According to the respondent No.1, the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-ML-0699 was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rash or negligence on the part of the driver of above offending Car.
Per- contra the petitioner was driving his car without taking any proper precautions and indication and suddenly came in a zig zag manner.
Hence, the accident was occurred due to negligence of the petitioner alone.
In order to substantiate the same, respondent No.1 has not placed positive evidence.
10. Further, to prove the alleged negligence on the part of the petitioner, the Insurance Company has cross-examined the petitioner/P.W.1 in detail.
Nothing has been elicited from mouth of P.W.1 to establish that the accident was took place due to his rash or negligent driving.
At the cost of repetition, to substantiate its contention, Insurance company has not placed positive evidence.

11. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".

12. Again it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that,
the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
13.
In the instant case, the petitioner has produced police documents.
As per Ex.P.1, complaint was lodged before the Kudur Police Station.
Thereafter, as per Ex.P.2, FIR was lodged against the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-ML- 0699.

On careful perusal of Ex.P.1, Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.5, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-ML-0699 and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.5 after completing investigation.
A careful perusal of Ex.P.4 and Ex.P.10, it reveals that, the car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MK-6492 was damaged.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.5 i.e., charge sheet,
it reveals that, the driver of offending vehicle i.e., Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51- ML-0699 has been arrayed as an accused.

14. At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, when the petitioner was driving his Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MK-6492, the driver of another Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-ML-0699 came in a reverse direction without indication in rash or negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the said Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MK-6492.

The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that driver of the Car Rajesh Prabhu M vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12171043/
4 bearing Reg.No.KA- 51-ML-0699 has caused the accident and damages to the Car belonging to petitioner.

sentences.text: Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.2:-
This issue is with regard to entitlement of the reliefs by the petitioner.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, the accident was caused due to the rash or negligent driving of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-ML- 0699 by its driver.
It is needless to mention that, 1st respondent is the insurer and the 2nd respondent is the R.C. owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
16. It is the case of the petitioner that, he is the R.C. owner of Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MK-6492 and the said car was damaged due to accident.
In order to substantiate the said contention, petitioner examined himself as P.W.1.
P.W.1 in his affidavit evidence has reiterated the petition averments.
Further P.W.1 has deposed that, his car was towed to Canara Auto Services Centre at J.P. Nagar, Bangalore by paying Rs.5,000/-.

Further deposed that, the engine bonnet,
front bumper, left side head light and indicator, front left side fender, front left side wheel, front left side door, front left side rear view mirror and other parts of his car were damaged and he has spent nearly a sum of Rs.2,95,826/- towards repair charges.
Further deposed that, he is the Assistant Consultant Doctor by profession and he used his car for both his personal as well as his profession.
After the accident he was engaged taxi by paying Rs.1,500/- per day and he could not use his car for one month.
Hence he has sustained loss towards transportation charges.
In support of his evidence P.W.1 has produced Ex.P.8, Ex.P.10, Ex.P.11 to Ex.P.14.
Ex . P.8
is the Notarized copy of R.C.
Ex.P.10 is the 12 photographs.
Ex . P.11
is the CD.
Ex . P.12
is the Tax Invoice.
Ex . P.13
is the 6 Receipts.
Ex. P.14
is the receipt pertaining to payment of towing chargs.
17. To prove the alleged damage and the repair work done to the car belonging to petitioner, he has examined one witness namely Girish Kumar S.V., Manager, Canara Auto Centre as P.W.2.
P.W.2 in his evidence deposed that, Ex.P.12 has been issued from his company.
Further stated that, the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MK-6492 was repaired by his company.
The expenses of repair amounts to Rs.2,95,862/-.
The said expenses was paid by the petitioner.
Thereafter P.W.2 was cross-examined from the side of 1 st respondent, nothing has been elicited to disbelieve the case of petitioner.
18. Accoding to petitioner he is the R.C. owner of Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MK-6492.
Ex.P.8 is the Notarized copy of R.C. Card and it reveals that, the petitioner is the R.C. owner of above said Car.
Ex.P.7 is the notarized copy of D.L. pertaining to petitioner.
Ex . P.9
the insurance policy pertaining to Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MK-6492.
It reveals that, the insurance policy was valid from 16.12.2022 to 15.12.2023.
Ex.P.12 is the Tax Invoice and it shows that, Canara Auto Centre has issued Tax Invoice towards repair cost of Rs.2,95,862/-.
On perusal of Ex.P.13, it reveals that, the petitioner has paid an amount of Rs.2,95,862/- to Canara Auto Centre towards repair of his Car.

As per Ex.P.14, it reveals that, petitioner has taken towing service and he has paid Rs.5,000/-
towards towing charges.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,95,862/- towards repair of his car and Rs.5,000/- towards towing charges.
In total the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,00,862/-.

sentences.text: Further P.W.1 has stated that, after the accident, for one month he could not use his car for personal use like to go to office and other purpose.
Further deposed that, each and every time he use to engage Taxi by paying Rs.1,500/- per day, hence he has suffered loss towards transportation charges.
In order to substantiate his contention, petitioner has not produced any bills for using hired vehicle.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any such expenses.
20. Regarding liability and interest.
Driving License:-
According to respondent No.1, the driver of offending vehicle has no valid driving licence to drive the vehicle.
However, respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence.
Charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that the driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.
Therefore, it appears to this Tribunal that, the driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid D.L. to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Insurance Policy and liability:-
In the instant case, respondent No.1 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-ML-0699.
Hence, the respondent No.1 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioner.

21. In view of the decision reported in MFA NO: 30131- 2019 dtd, 12.5.2020 and M.F.A.No.100090/2014 C/w M.F.A.No.25107/2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and Others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and Another, rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition.

sentences.text: Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the Partly Affirmative.
22. ISSUE No.3:- In view of discussions made above, I proceed to pass the following.

:ORDER:
Claim petition filed by the Petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the petition.
Petitioner is awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.3,00,862/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Eight Hundred and Sixty Two only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.
Respondent No.1 shall deposit the compensation in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award Accordingly.
